artifacts.summary: Confirms the exact single-candidate resolution site in validate-artifact.sh, the existing verification_scope_project_suite_roots reader, and designs a sibling-lib.sh candidate-list extension plus corpus-naming warning text and three new test cases, with no change to suite-selection-lib.sh itself.

memory_candidates.content: scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh fixes its own scripts-root/tests-dir (_SSL_SCRIPTS_ROOT/_SSL_TESTS_DIR) once at source time, derived purely from its own ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} location two directories up -- there is no parameter or env override. The only way to re-root the exact same, unmodified selection engine at a different corpus is to source a DIFFERENT on-disk copy of the same file that lives inside that corpus's own tree (a lib/+tests/ mirror). This generalizes beyond validate-artifact.sh: any future caller wanting a non-default corpus from this library must locate and source an alternate copy, never override its internal _SSL_-prefixed variables (explicitly not part of its public contract).

verification_scope.project_suite_roots (scripts/lib/verification-scope-lib.sh) is schema-generic ('a non-shell test corpus, for example') -- it carries NO structural guarantee that a declared root mirrors the agent-system's own lib/+tests/ scripts-tree shape. Any consumer that wants to reuse an existing shell-suite engine (like suite-selection-lib.sh) against a declared project_suite_root must derive a candidate path assuming that mirror shape and gracefully degrade to a fallback + named warning when it's absent -- never treat a non-mirrored declared root as an error.
